Chapter 14. Living the Questions.
Life’s always throwing questions our way, isn’t it? Some are big, some are small. Some demand answers right now, while others just linger in the back of our minds. Most of us? We want answers. We crave solutions and certainty. But here’s the thing—Zen flips that idea on its head. Instead of chasing after answers, Zen asks us to actually live the questions.
Picture yourself standing at a crossroads, not really sure which path to take. Your mind’s probably racing, trying to figure out the “right” choice. But imagine if, instead, you let the question breathe. What if you gave it space to unfold at its own pace?
Zen stories love to highlight this. There’s one where a student asks, “What is the meaning of life?” And the teacher just says, “Go wash your bowl.” It’s not really an answer, right? It’s more of an invitation—to drop back into the present moment.
Most people try to tie up loose ends as quickly as possible, desperate to move from uncertainty to certainty. But Zen encourages us to see questions not as problems to be solved, but as mysteries to be experienced. If you can stick with a question—really live with it—sometimes, surprising new possibilities open up. You start to see things differently.
In everyday life, this might just mean having a little more patience with uncertainty. Letting things unfold in their own good time. It could mean being open to new experiences, or seeing the world through fresh eyes. Trusting that, when you truly need an answer, it’ll show up.
Over time, living the questions can actually become a real strength. There’s a freedom in not needing to have everything figured out right away. You meet each moment with curiosity, and the world feels a little less intimidating—maybe even a bit more magical. There’s wonder in the not knowing. There’s joy in the possibilities.
Zen doesn’t hand out answers. But it does offer a way to be with the questions. And by living them, you just might find a quiet kind of peace in the midst of uncertainty. Wisdom tends to bloom right in the heart of that mystery.
